Quick answers to your questions up front:
- Customer-managed keys (KMS): Yes — Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via supported KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for data at rest. For on-prem / air-gapped installs we support HSM integrations; Marcus can share specifics.

Hi Anna / ACME team — following up with the architecture and security notes. High-level summary below and attached diagram.

High-level VPC deployment options:
1) Dedicated VPC (recommended for production):
   - We provision Redwood Private control plane in a customer VPC via a private-managed deployment; model runtime lives in dedicated subnets with strict egress rules.
   - KMS: Customer-managed keys (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) for encryption at rest; we can also integrate with customer HSMs for on-prem.
   - Network isolation: No public ingress to runtime nodes; only a private NAT and designated management bastion/VPN.
   - Audit logs: Forwarded to your SIEM over TLS to a collector inside your VPC.

2) Air-gapped / on-prem option (for highest regulatory assurance):
   - Full on-prem package that can be deployed in an isolated network with no outbound internet.
   - KMS via on-prem HSM; all telemetry optionally retained locally.
   - Recommended when you need physical separation for regulated data or to meet specific audit controls.

Notes on vendor SSQ: we pre-filled common responses in the attached SSQ and flagged items that require legal review (third-party subprocessors, BAA).

Attachments:
- redwood_vpc_deployment_diagram.png (PNG)
- completed_vendor_ssq_answers.xlsx (Excel)

Next steps:
- Confirm which option (Dedicated VPC vs Air-gapped) you'd like us to model in the architecture review.
- We'll bring a short checklist for BAA and SOC 2 artifacts during the call.

If helpful, we can also include a short cost/ops delta between Dedicated VPC vs Air-gapped options.

Cheers,
